st.3: The huddled skeletons at Mohenjodaro are now read as evidence of a massacre.

x: 1, 2 and 4 are correct. 3 is wrong: the huddled skeletons at Mohenjodaro, once read as a massacre, are now read as multiple burials. Kalibangan's three burial types (incl. skeleton-less circular pits) and Rakhigarhi's 56 skeletons are correct.
Iron axes with fire cleared the Gangetic forests, and Taxila is listed among the early iron sites (c. 1000 BC).

st.3: The Taittiriya Brahmana gives the theory of the divine origin of kingship.

x: All three are correct. The Aitareya Brahmana gives the earliest account (the gods, losing to the Asuras, chose a king) and sees the king as protector of Brahmins; the Taittiriya Brahmana gives the divine origin of kingship.

st.1: It was denied to Shudras and women.

x: Both are correct. Upanayana was the sacred-thread initiation into Vedic study for Brahmanas, Kshatriyas and Vaishyas; Shudras and women were excluded from it.

st.3: The BHU re-study of Rajghat places urban Varanasi at c. 800 BCE.

x: All three are correct. Over 60 towns flourished in the Ganga region in 600–300 BCE, Rajghat has yielded punch-marked coins and Greek-inscribed seals, and the BHU re-study (Sep 2026) puts urban Varanasi at c. 800 BCE.

st.3: After the Buddha's death his relics were divided and enshrined in stupas, solid mounds worshipped by circumambulation.

x: All three are correct. The Amaravati Mahachaitya is the largest stupa in AP and South India, Kesariya is the largest and tallest excavated stupa (ASI), and the Buddha's relics were divided and enshrined in stupas after his death.

st.3: The Mehrauli Iron Pillar refers to him as 'Chandra'.

x: All three are correct. Vikramaditya (linked with the Saka victory) was also used by Skandagupta; Devagupta and Devaraja are known from Sanchi and Vakataka records; the Mehrauli pillar calls him 'Chandra'.

st.2: Sulka was the customs duty and toll on merchandise.
st.3: Sita, the revenue from crown land, was collected only in cash.

x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: Sita, the revenue from crown land, was the produce of those lands collected in kind; the tax paid in cash was Hiranya.

st.3: At Nalanda he studied the Yogashastra under Silabhadra.
st.4: Besides Harsha and Pulakesin II, he praised the Pallava Mahendravarman I.

x: 1, 2 and 3 are correct. 4 is wrong: the Pallava king Hiuen Tsang praised was Narasimhavarman I, not Mahendravarman I. He left Changan in 629, returned about 16 years later and studied the Yogashastra under Silabhadra.

st.1: Teaching was conducted mainly in Sanskrit.

x: Both are correct. Nalanda had a difficult entrance examination and used Sanskrit as the medium of instruction.

st.2: He gave the province of Badakhshan to Kamran.
st.3: He ruled through the Mansabdari system.

x: 1 and 4 are correct. 2 is wrong: Badakhshan was given to Humayun. 3 is wrong: Babur ruled through jagirs and parganas; the Mansabdari system was Akbar's. His empire reached the borders of Bihar; he died at Agra and was later buried at Bagh-e-Babur, Kabul.

st.4: One rupiya was worth 64 dams.

x: All four are correct. The rupiya was silver (about 178 grains), the dam copper and the mohur gold, and the rupiya-dam ratio was 1 : 64.

st.2: Jagirdars' rights over their assignments were hereditary and saleable.

x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: jagirs were not hereditary and were often transferred; it was zamindari rights that were hereditary and saleable.

st.2: His father Maha Singh was the chief of the Sukerchakia misl.

x: All four are correct. Ranjit Singh was born at Gujranwala (1780); his father Maha Singh headed the Sukerchakia misl; his Lahore high court was the Adalat-i-Ala; he got the Kohinoor from Shah Shuja in 1813.

st.2: The Bhakti movement brought Hindus and Muslims closer and ended the caste system.

x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: the movement weakened caste and brought Hindus and Muslims closer, but it did not end the caste system. Ramananda was the first medieval reformer to denounce caste outright, and Palnati Brahmanayudu's Chapakudu was common dining for all castes.

st.3: He is held to be an incarnation of Adisesha.

x: All four are correct. Ramanuja, held to be an incarnation of Adisesha, was centred at Srirangam, was called Ilaya Azhwar and was the first true exponent of Bhakti in reaction to Shankara's Advaita.

st.3: Jalaluddin Tabrizi belonged to the Chishti order.

x: 1, 2 and 4 are correct. 3 is wrong: Jalaluddin Tabrizi was a Suhrawardi saint, not a Chishti. Shihabuddin Suhrawardi of Baghdad founded the order, the Firdausi order flourished in Bihar, and Bahauddin Zakariya got the title Shaikh-ul-Islam for backing Iltutmish.

st.2: Nizamuddin Auliya was the disciple of Baba Farid.

x: All four are correct. The chain runs Usman Harooni - Moinuddin - Bakhtiyar Kaki - Baba Farid - Nizamuddin; Amir Khusrau was Nizamuddin's disciple and Alauddin Sabir Kaliyari was Farid's other main disciple.

st.1: It was begun by Vasco da Gama in 1502 and later systematised by Albuquerque.

x: All three are correct. The cartaz (a naval trade pass) was begun by Vasco da Gama in 1502 and systematised by Albuquerque; ships without it were confiscated and crews punished, and it was backed by the cafila convoy.

st.2: Azimullah Khan was known as "Danka Shah".

x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: Azimullah Khan was called "Krantidoot"; "Danka Shah" was Maulvi Ahmadullah Shah of Faizabad.

st.1: At Kanpur, Sir Hugh Wheeler had surrendered before the city was retaken by Colin Campbell.

x: All three are correct. Sir Hugh Wheeler surrendered at Kanpur, Canning declared peace on 8 July 1858, and Colin Campbell (later Lord Clyde) became Commander-in-Chief after Anson's death.

st.2: Lord Stanley was the first Secretary of State for India under the Government of India Act 1858.

x: All three are correct. Canning withdrew the Doctrine of Lapse and called the princes "breakwaters to the storm"; Lord Stanley was the first Secretary of State for India; Bentinck was the first Governor-General of India under the Charter Act 1833.

st.3: He received Banaras and Kora.

x: 1, 2 and 4 are correct. 3 is wrong: Shah Alam received Kora and Allahabad; Banaras was left to Balwant Singh, not given to him.

st.3: Hastings later stopped the Rs 26 lakh payment to Shah Alam and sold Kora and Allahabad to the Nawab of Awadh.

x: All three are correct. Clive returned as Governor of Bengal in May 1765, Warren Hastings became Governor in 1772, and Hastings stopped Shah Alam's Rs 26 lakh and sold Kora and Allahabad to Awadh.

st.3: The Company paid the Nawab of Awadh Rs 53 lakh for the nizamat.

x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: the Rs 53 lakh for the nizamat was paid to the Nawab of Bengal, not the Nawab of Awadh, who instead paid a Rs 50 lakh war indemnity.

st.2: A Jacobin Club was founded at Seringapatam in 1797, and he became 'Citizen Tipu'.

x: All three are correct. Tipu set up a Board of Admiralty (1796), backed the Jacobin Club at Seringapatam (1797) as 'Citizen Tipu', and pioneered war rockets with a new calendar, coinage and sericulture.

st.1: The 1809 treaty of 'eternal friendship' with Sindh was made under Lord Bentinck.

x: 2 and 3 are correct. 1 is wrong: the 1809 treaty was made under Lord Minto; Pottinger's treaty (1832) came under Bentinck.

st.2: It created the Board of Control to supervise the Company's affairs.

x: 1, 3 and 4 are correct. 2 is wrong: the Board of Control was created by Pitt's India Act of 1784; the 1813 Act renewed the charter for 20 years.

All three are correct: the Circars came in 1765-66; 1802 saw the Permanent Settlement in the Circars (Vizianagaram peshcush Rs 6 lakh) and Ryotwari in Rayalaseema; Uyyalawada's 1846 revolt hit the Koilkuntla treasury.

st.2: The first railway line in Andhra, Puttur–Renigunta, was opened in 1862.
st.3: The Dutch set up their first factory in Andhra at Bhimunipatnam.

x: 1, 2 and 4 are correct. 3 is wrong: the first Dutch factory in Andhra was at Machilipatnam, not Bhimunipatnam. Nellore was known for mica, Puttur–Renigunta opened in 1862, and jute mills came up at Chittivalasa and Nellimarla.

st.4: He launched the Self-Respect Movement before he joined the Congress.

x: 1, 2 and 3 are correct. 4 is wrong: he launched the Self-Respect Movement in 1925, after leaving the Congress, which he had joined in 1920.

st.2: He was principal of Pithapuram Raja's College, Kakinada, and the first Telugu Vice-Chancellor of Madras University.

x: All three are correct. He was knighted in 1924, was principal of Pithapuram Raja's College and the first Telugu Vice-Chancellor of Madras University, and ran Brahma Prakasika; C.R. Reddy was the first VC of Andhra University.

st.3: The 2021 proposal to raise the marriage age of women to 21 has not become law.

x: All four are correct. The age of consent rose to 14 (1925) and 16 (1949), the 1978 amendment set 18/21, the 2021 proposal has not become law (as of 2026), and Sleeman suppressed Thuggee in the 1830s.

st.3: G.D. Birla was its first president and Amritlal Thakkar its secretary.

x: All three are correct. Gandhi founded it on 30 September 1932 in Yerawada prison, it was first the All India Anti-Untouchability League, and G.D. Birla was president with Amritlal Thakkar (Thakkar Bapa) as secretary.

st.3: The Manusmriti was burnt at Mahad on 25 December 1927.

x: All four are correct. The Bole Resolution (1923), the Chavdar Tank satyagraha at Mahad (20 March 1927), the Manusmriti Dahan at Mahad (25 December 1927) and the Kalaram Temple Satyagraha at Nashik (1930–35).

st.1: It was anti-British.

x: Both are correct. The Wahabi Movement was anti-British; in Hyderabad it was led by Mubariz-ud-Daulah.

st.3: Bhagat Singh fired the first shot at Saunders.

x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: Rajguru fired the first shot, then Bhagat Singh, while Azad covered the retreat.

st.1: The Gandhi-Irwin Pact, which paved the way for the Second RTC, was signed on 5 March 1931.

x: All three are correct. The Gandhi-Irwin Pact (5 March 1931) paved the way for the Second RTC; the First RTC was opened by George V and chaired by MacDonald; the Third had only 46 delegates and was followed by the 1933 White Paper.

st.2: Under the 'crawling order' Indians had to crawl down the Amritsar lane where the missionary Marcella Sherwood had been assaulted.

x: All three are correct. Martial law was proclaimed in Punjab, the crawling order applied to the lane where Marcella Sherwood was assaulted, and the massacre was a background to Non-Cooperation (1920).

st.1: Gandhi's letter of 2 March 1930 informed Irwin of the planned Salt March.

x: All three are correct. Gandhi's eleven demands went to Irwin on 31 January 1930, the CWC gave him full powers in February, and his letter of 2 March 1930 informed Irwin of the Salt March, which began on 12 March.

st.2: Lord Linlithgow was the Viceroy when the movement was launched.

x: All three are correct. Rangoon fell in March 1942, Lord Linlithgow was Viceroy in August 1942 (Wavell came only in October 1943), and price rises and rice and salt shortages fed discontent.

st.2: Dwarabandala Chandrayya and Ambul Reddy led the Rampa revolt of 1879-80.

x: All four are correct. The 1879-80 Rampa revolt was against Mansabdar Madhava Bhupati and was led by Dwarabandala Chandrayya and Ambul Reddy (Alluri was born only in 1897); the Rekapalli revolt arose from a higher axe tax on podu in a famine.

st.3: The term "Gandhian Innovation" was coined by C.K. Prahalad and R.A. Mashelkar.

x: All three are correct. Production for need, not profit; Ram Rajya as people's sovereignty on moral authority; and "Gandhian Innovation" (more from less for more people) coined by C.K. Prahalad and R.A. Mashelkar.

st.1: Volunteers of the Eluru National School joined the movement in May 1930.

x: All three are correct. Eluru National School volunteers joined in May 1930; in towns the movement meant picketing foreign-cloth shops, and in villages salt-making, cutting toddy palms and raiding salt depots.

st.2: It was enacted on the recommendation of the Subba Rao Committee.

x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: the Subba Rao Committee lay behind the AP (Andhra Area) Tenancy Act, 1956; the 1950 Hyderabad Act came in the context of the Telangana armed struggle and let tenants buy ownership at 60% of the price.

st.2: Its Deputy Chief Minister was K.V. Ranga Reddy.

x: 1, 3 and 4 are correct. 2 is wrong: N. Sanjiva Reddy was Deputy CM of Andhra State; K.V. Ranga Reddy was Deputy CM of Andhra Pradesh (1956).

st.3: The women's session at Kakinada in 1916 was presided over by Achanta Rukmini Lakshmipathi.
st.4: The Nellore session of 1917 accepted the inclusion of Madras city in the Andhra demand.

x: 1, 2 and 3 are correct. 4 is wrong: the Nellore session (1917) rejected, not accepted, the Madras city demand. The 1916 women's session was led by Achanta Rukmini Lakshmipathi.

st.2: The one-man Girglani Commission was set up in 2001 by the Chandrababu Naidu government.

st.3: Lahuradeva is in Bihar.

x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: Lahuradeva is in Uttar Pradesh, not Bihar; Koldihwa (Belan valley, UP) was earlier thought to have the oldest rice.

st.3: Yajnasri Satakarni was the last king of the dynasty.

x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: Yajnasri Satakarni (27th in the Matsya list) was the greatest of the later kings, but the last king was Pulomavi III (30th).

st.3: Muslin and pearls were exported.

x: All three are correct. Muslin, spices, pearls, diamonds and ivory were exported, while gold, wine (from Italy and Arabia), silk and camphor (from China) came in.

st.3: His reign is called the golden age of Prakrit.

x: All four are correct. Hala honoured Kumarila and Sripalita, married Lilavati of Sri Lanka, and his reign is the golden age of Prakrit; his Gathasaptasati is a source for society rather than political history.

st.2: No gold coins were issued; gold was used only as bullion.

x: Both are correct. Lead was the most common metal; the Satavahanas issued no gold coins and used gold only as bullion.

st.1: Its kings performed Vedic sacrifices while its queens patronised Buddhism.

x: All three are correct. Ikshvaku kings performed Vedic sacrifices while their queens patronised Buddhism; the dynasty was a bridge dynasty and brought the Amaravati school to its peak.

st.1: The AMASR Act was enacted in 1958.

x: Both are correct. The AMASR Act is of 1958 (1972 is the Antiquities and Art Treasures Act), and ICOMOS dates from 1965.

st.2: Veerabhadra Vijayam is a work of Bammera Potana.
st.3: Kashikhandam was written at the request of Kataya Vema.

x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: Kashikhandam was dedicated to Veerabhadra Reddi of Rajahmundry (c. 1440), not Kataya Vema (d. 1414). Veerabhadra Vijayam is by Bammera Potana, not Srinatha.

st.3: It was found by J.S. Fleet.

x: All three are correct. The Anumakonda inscription records Kakatiya independence (1163) under Rudradeva, was composed by Achitendru and was found by J.S. Fleet.

st.2: Amir Khusrau calls Prataparudra 'Ravaddar Dev'.
st.3: Sakalya Malla was a court poet of Ganapatideva.

x: 1, 2 and 4 are correct. 3 is wrong: Sakalya Malla was a court poet of Prataparudra II, not Ganapatideva. Khusrau's Khazain-ul-Futuh describes the double-walled Warangal fort and calls Prataparudra 'Ravaddar Dev'.

st.3: In 1311 Kakatiya troops under Pedarudru joined Malik Kafur's march on Madurai.

x: 1, 2 and 4 are correct. 3 is wrong: the Kakatiya troops that joined Kafur's march on Madurai in 1311 were under Muppidi Nayaka, not Pedarudru.

st.3: Kondavidu lies in Guntur district.

x: All four are correct. The capitals ran Addanki - Kondaveedu - Rajamahendravaram; the Manyapuram inscription records Anavota Reddi's shift to Kondavidu, which lies in Guntur (near Chilakaluripet); Kondapalli fort is credited to Prolaya Vema.

st.1: His wife Chand Sultana was the sister of Abdullah Qutb Shah.

x: 2 and 3 are correct. 1 is wrong: Chand Sultana was the sister of Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah, not Abdullah Qutb Shah. Ibrahim Adil Shah II wrote the Kitab-i-Nauras, founded Nauraspur and received Firishta's dedication.

st.3: Meruka was a tax on the sale and purchase of goods.

x: All four are correct. Saluva Narasimha first remitted the marriage tax, santhalu rights were auctioned to the Sunkandarlu, Meruka was the sale-purchase tax (Mera was the Ayagars' share), and Merulu were the Talari's grain gifts.
All three are correct: Rama Raya was Sadasiva's regent, razed Ahmadnagar with Bijapur in 1557-63 and sheltered Jagadeva Rao.

st.1: Caesar Frederick, a Venetian traveller, saw the ruined city in 1567.

x: All three are correct. The Venetian Caesar Frederick saw the ruins in 1567, Colin Mackenzie mapped Hampi in 1800 and became the first Surveyor General, and Sewell wrote A Forgotten Empire (1900).

st.2: Mir Jumla was killed in this battle.

x: Only 1 is correct. 2 is wrong: Jagga Raya, not Mir Jumla, was killed at Toppur (1616); Mir Jumla later defeated Sriranga III at Vandavasi (1642).

st.4: The early English got their silk and cotton piece-goods mainly from Bengal.

x: All four are correct. Chintz brightened after washing, saltpetre went out from Machilipatnam, Narsapur and Pulicat, the Koh-i-Noor came from Kollur (Guntur), and the early English got silk and cotton piece-goods mainly from Bengal.

st.2: P. Sundarayya was its secretary at the founding.

x: Both are correct. The Andhra Communist Party was formally founded at Kakinada in January 1936 with P. Sundarayya as secretary.

st.4: The Oudh Kisan Sabha of 1920 was set up by Baba Ramchandra and Jawaharlal Nehru, not by him.

x: All four are correct. Sahajanand founded the Bihar Provincial Kisan Sabha (1929), ran the Hindi weekly Hunkar from Patna and formed the All India United Kisan Sabha before his death (1950); the Oudh Kisan Sabha (1920) was the work of Baba Ramchandra and Nehru.

st.2: The pledge "Bharata Desam Naa Matrubhoomi" was written by Paidimarri Venkata Subbarao.

x: All three are correct. "Desamunu preminchumanna" is from Gurajada's Mutyala Saralu (1910), the pledge is by Paidimarri Venkata Subbarao, and spoken-Telugu songs reached villagers whom pamphlets could not.

st.3: Andhrula Charitramu, which it published in 1910, was written by Chilukuri Veerabhadra Rao.

x: All three are correct. The Mandali was founded at Hyderabad in 1906 by Komarraju Lakshmana Rao with the Munagala Zamindar's support; Gadicherla and Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao were co-founders / secretaries; Andhrula Charitramu (1910) was by Chilukuri Veerabhadra Rao.

st.3: A traditional troupe has three performers.

x: All four are correct. Burrakatha is Thandana Katha in Rayalaseema, Guntur is its birthplace, a troupe is of three (narrator and two Vantalu), and its instruments include the Gummata, Burra, Tambura and Ukki.

st.2: Machilipatnam-Pedana Kalamkari is the block-printed style of the craft.

x: All four are correct. Kondapalli toys (NTR district) use Tella Poniki wood, Machilipatnam-Pedana Kalamkari is block-printed (the freehand pen style is Srikalahasti's), and Etikoppaka toys are from Anakapalli district.
The Anandapuram base secures the LWE corridor of the ASR and Parvathipuram Manyam districts, both in north coastal Andhra Pradesh.

st.2: Beti Bachao Beti Padhao, now covering all 26 districts, was launched in 2015.

x: All three are correct. The 181 Women Helpline dates from 2016, Beti Bachao Beti Padhao was launched in 2015, and the Sashakt Panchayat Netri Abhiyan is for women elected representatives.

st.3: The Indo-Greeks issued gold coins in India before the Kushanas.

x: All three are correct. Indo-Greek coins were mostly silver and copper and reveal 30+ kings; the Indo-Greeks issued the first gold coins, and the Kushanas later issued gold on a large scale.

st.2: The first gold coins in India were issued by the Indo-Greeks.

x: All three are correct. The Indo-Greeks first issued coins attributable to kings and the first (rare) gold coins, which the Kushanas later issued on a large scale; their bilingual coins carry Greek and Kharoshthi Prakrit.

st.4: As per SRS 2024, Bihar has the lowest TFR among States.

x: 1, 2 and 3 are correct. 4 is wrong: per SRS 2024 Delhi (1.2) has the lowest TFR; Bihar has the highest, not the lowest.

st.2: The ILO (2022) estimated that India's gig workforce will reach 2.35 crore by 2029-30.

x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: the 2.35 crore by 2029-30 projection is NITI Aayog's (2022), not the ILO's. Keith Hart coined 'informal sector' and gig workers numbered about 77 lakh in 2020-21.

st.2: According to PLFS 2020-21, men formed the majority of India's migrants.
st.4: Migration and Mobility Partnerships are signed by the Ministry of Labour and Employment.

x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: PLFS 2020-21 put migrants at 28.9% of the population, and women (mostly migrating for marriage) far outnumber men. 4 is wrong: Migration and Mobility Partnerships are signed by the MEA, not the Labour Ministry.

st.2: Gandharva marriage, illustrated by Shakuntala and Dushyanta, is one of the four approved forms.

x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: Gandharva marriage (by mutual consent, Shakuntala–Dushyanta) is a disapproved form, only conditionally accepted.

st.1: M.N. Srinivas first called the process "Westernisation".
st.2: Only the twice-born castes, never the local dominant caste, serve as the reference group.

x: Only 3 is correct. 1 is wrong: Srinivas first called it "Brahminisation" (Coorgs study, 1952). 2 is wrong: besides the twice-born castes, the local dominant caste can also be the reference group.

st.1: Paul Brass is associated with the constructivist view that identity is kept by boundaries.
st.2: Clifford Geertz and Edward Shils are associated with the instrumentalist view.

x: Only 3 is correct. 1 is wrong: Paul Brass is an instrumentalist (elites mobilise identity for power). 2 is wrong: Geertz and Shils are primordialists. Barth and Anderson are constructivists.

st.2: The expression 'untouchability' is defined in the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955.
st.3: Under Article 35(a)(ii), both Parliament and the State Legislatures can prescribe punishment for offences under Article 17.

x: Only 1 is correct. 2 is wrong: 'untouchability' is defined neither in the Constitution nor in any Act. 3 is wrong: under Article 35(a)(ii) only Parliament, not the State Legislatures, can prescribe punishment for Article 17 offences.

st.1: Bhagya Reddy Varma praised the Harijan Sevak Sangh as the model for Dalit uplift.

x: 2 and 3 are correct. 1 is wrong: Bhagya Reddy Varma criticised the Harijan Sevak Sangh as paternalistic, not praised it.

st.4: The literacy rate of Andhra Pradesh as per Census 2011 was above the national average.

x: 1, 2 and 3 are correct. 4 is wrong: AP's literacy in 2011 was 67.35%, below the national average (about 74%).

st.3: It replaced the term 'child' with 'juvenile'.

x: 1, 2 and 4 are correct. 3 is wrong: the Act did the reverse, replacing 'juvenile' with 'child' / 'child in conflict with law'.

st.2: The Syama Prasad Mookerjee Research Foundation is linked to the Congress.

x: 1, 3 and 4 are correct. 2 is wrong: the Syama Prasad Mookerjee Research Foundation is BJP-linked; the Rajiv Gandhi Foundation is Congress-linked.

st.1: Mission Vatsalya subsumed the Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS) scheme.
st.3: The Scheme for Adolescent Girls is a part of Mission Shakti.

x: Only 2 is correct. 1 is wrong: Mission Vatsalya subsumed the Integrated Child Protection Scheme (ICPS), not ICDS, which is under Saksham Anganwadi. 3 is wrong: the Scheme for Adolescent Girls is part of Saksham Anganwadi & Poshan 2.0, not Mission Shakti.

st.1: The Samarthya sub-scheme deals with women's safety and includes the 24x7 Women Helpline 181.
st.3: PMMVY falls under the Sambal sub-scheme.

x: 2 and 4 are correct. 1 is wrong: women's safety and Helpline 181 come under Sambal, not Samarthya. 3 is wrong: PMMVY falls under Samarthya (empowerment), not Sambal.

st.1: It set up the Employees' State Insurance Corporation.
st.2: The Atal Pension Yojana is listed in its Schedule I.

x: Only 3 is correct. 1 is wrong: the 2008 Act set up the National Social Security Board; ESIC dates from the ESI Act, 1948. 2 is wrong: Schedule I lists IGNOAPS, NFBS, JSY, Janashree Bima, AABY and RSBY, not APY.

st.3: Under PMVBRY, the incentive for first-time employees is paid to their employers, not to the employees.
st.4: The Ashraya Bima Yojana (2001) was a pension scheme for retired workers.

st.2: AP's monthly pension for persons with disabilities is the same as its old-age pension.

st.2: The first draft of the Constitution (October 1947), with 243 Articles and 13 Schedules, was prepared by B.R. Ambedkar.
st.3: B.N. Rau later served as a judge of the Permanent Court of Arbitration.

st.4: The ideal of a Republic was borrowed from the USA.

x: Only 1 is correct. 2 is wrong: the CAA covers migrants from Afghanistan, Bangladesh and Pakistan, not Sri Lanka (entry by 31 December 2014). 3 is wrong: citizenship counts from the date of entry into India. 4 is wrong: both Sixth Schedule areas and ILP areas are exempted.

st.2: It is a source of power to the legislature.

st.1: In February 2026, in Mritunjay Tiwari v. Union of India, the Court questioned the caste-discrimination clause of the AICTE regulations.

x: Only 2 is correct. 1 is wrong: Mritunjay Tiwari (Feb 2026) concerned the UGC equity regulations, not AICTE.

st.2: The Right to Freedom group consists of Articles 14 to 18.
st.3: The right to acquire, hold and dispose of property under Article 19(1)(f) was deleted by the 42nd Amendment.

x: Only 1 is correct. 2 is wrong: the Right to Freedom group is Articles 19–22; Articles 14–18 are the Right to Equality. 3 is wrong: Art. 19(1)(f) was deleted by the 44th Amendment (1978), not the 42nd.

st.2: A Special Public Prosecutor is appointed by the National Human Rights Commission.
st.3: 'Public servant' has the meaning given in Section 21 of the Code of Criminal Procedure.

x: 1 and 4 are correct. 2 is wrong: under Sec. 31 the State Government specifies or appoints the Special Public Prosecutor (an advocate of at least 7 years' practice). 3 is wrong: 'public servant' has the meaning in Sec. 21 IPC (now Sec. 2(28) BNS), not the CrPC.

st.1: Goa follows the French Civil Code, retained after its liberation.
st.2: Gujarat was the first State to bring a State Uniform Civil Code into force.
st.4: Article 44 is enforceable in court like a Fundamental Right.

x: Only 3 is correct. 1 is wrong: Goa follows the Portuguese Civil Code of 1867. 2 is wrong: Uttarakhand was first (27 Jan 2025), Gujarat second. 4 is wrong: Art. 44 is a Directive Principle, not enforceable in court.

st.2: The 1978 joint sitting was on the Prevention of Terrorism Bill.

x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: the 1978 joint sitting was on the Banking Service Commission (Repeal) Bill; POTA was the 2002 sitting.

st.1: After the Berubari reference (1960), the cession of Berubari could be made by a simple law under Article 3.
st.3: Katchatheevu was transferred to Sri Lanka by the 100th Constitutional Amendment.

x: Only 2 is correct. 1 is wrong: cession needed an Article 368 amendment (the 9th Amendment, 1960), not an Article 3 law. 3 is wrong: Katchatheevu went by the 1974–76 agreements with no amendment; the 100th Amendment gave effect to the India–Bangladesh LBA.

st.4: Tripura has more seats in the Rajya Sabha than in the Lok Sabha.

x: 1, 2 and 3 are correct. 4 is wrong: Tripura has 2 Lok Sabha seats and only 1 Rajya Sabha seat.

st.2: Nargis Dutt was the first woman nominated to the Rajya Sabha.

x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: Rukmini Devi Arundale (1952) was the first woman nominated; Nargis Dutt was the first film actress nominated.

st.2: A vote against the party whip does not disqualify a member if the Speaker or Chairman condones it within 15 days.

x: 1, 3 and 4 are correct. 2 is wrong: the vote against the whip must be condoned by the member's political party (within 15 days), not by the presiding officer.

st.1: An ordinance promulgated by the President lapses six weeks after it is promulgated.
st.3: In Krishna Kumar Singh (2017), a seven-judge bench held that laying an ordinance before the legislature is not mandatory.
st.4: The President may withhold assent to a Constitution Amendment Bill.

x: Only 2 is correct. 1 is wrong: an ordinance lapses six weeks after Parliament reassembles, not after promulgation. 3 is wrong: the seven-judge bench held laying to be mandatory. 4 is wrong: since the 24th Amendment (1971) the President must give assent to an amendment Bill.

st.3: The Constitution specifies 'proved misbehaviour' as the ground for removing the Vice-President.

x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: the Constitution specifies no ground for removing the Vice-President (a Rajya Sabha resolution agreed to by the Lok Sabha).

st.2: The Department of Personnel was set up in 1966, before the Administrative Reforms Commission was appointed.

x: Only 1 is correct. 2 is wrong: the Administrative Reforms Commission came first (1966), and the Department of Personnel followed in 1970.

st.1: Under Section 8 of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014, the Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh had a special responsibility for law and order in the common capital, Hyderabad.
st.3: The Andhra Pradesh government of 2019-24, under N. Chandrababu Naidu, had five Deputy Chief Ministers.

x: Only 2 is correct. 1 is wrong: the Sec. 8 special responsibility for Hyderabad was the Governor's, not a Chief Minister's. 3 is wrong: the 2019-24 government with five Deputy CMs was that of Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy.

st.1: The post is created by Article 164(1A) of the Constitution.

x: 2 and 3 are correct. 1 is wrong: the Deputy CM is not mentioned in the Constitution; Art. 164(1A) is the 15 per cent cap on the size of the Ministry.

st.2: The Chief Minister addresses his resignation to the President.
st.3: State Ministers hold office during the pleasure of the Chief Minister.

x: 1 and 4 are correct. 2 is wrong: the resignation goes to the Governor. 3 is wrong: under Art. 164(1) Ministers hold office during the pleasure of the Governor.

st.2: The Constitution requires him to resign when the Council of Ministers resigns.

x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: he resigns with the government only by convention, not under any constitutional requirement.

st.2: The separate National Commission for Scheduled Tribes is a statutory body set up by an Act of Parliament.
st.3: The National Commission for Backward Classes was given constitutional status under Article 338A.

x: Only 1 is correct. 2 is wrong: the NCST (19 Feb 2004) is a constitutional body under Art. 338A, created by the 89th Amendment. 3 is wrong: the NCBC got constitutional status under Art. 338B (102nd Amendment, 2018).

st.1: It was established in 1955 under Article 343.

x: Only 2 is correct. 1 is wrong: the commission (1955) was set up under Article 344, not Article 343; it was headed by B.G. Kher.

st.3: It is a constitutional body set up under Article 263.

x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: the NEC is a statutory body under the NEC Act, 1971, not a constitutional body under Art. 263.

st.2: The 2015 sub-group on Swachh Bharat was convened by Parkash Singh Badal.

x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: N. Chandrababu Naidu convened the Swachh Bharat sub-group; Parkash Singh Badal convened Skill Development.

st.2: It measures only the financial devolution to panchayats.

x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: the Index measures six dimensions (including Capacity Enhancement and Accountability), not finances alone.

st.3: Tribal MMR and IMR are below the State average.

x: 1, 2 and 4 are correct. 3 is wrong: tribal MMR and IMR are above, not below, the State average.

st.2: Its draft plan is forwarded to the State Government by the District Collector.

x: 1, 3 and 4 are correct. 2 is wrong: the DPC's draft plan is sent to the State Government by its chairperson, not the Collector.

st.2: Its first Deputy Chairman was Gulzarilal Nanda, and the Deputy Chairman held the rank of a Minister of State.
st.3: The 1950 resolution was repealed by an Act of Parliament in 2014.

x: Only 1 is correct. 2 is wrong: the Deputy Chairman had Cabinet Minister rank, not MoS rank. 3 is wrong: the 1950 resolution was repealed by the Union Cabinet on 13 August 2014, not by an Act.

st.1: The Planning Commission followed a bottom-up approach to planning.

x: Only 2 is correct. 1 is wrong: the Planning Commission followed a top-down approach (NITI Aayog stresses bottom-up, cooperative planning); both bodies rest on Cabinet resolutions.

st.3: The Miniratna category was created along with the Maharatna category in 2010.
st.4: Nine PSUs were made Maharatnas with greater autonomy in 1997.

x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: the Miniratna category dates from 1997, with the Navratnas; only Maharatna dates from 2010. 4 is wrong: the nine PSUs of 1997 were made Navratnas, not Maharatnas.

st.3: It was associated with the IMF, the World Bank and the WTO.

x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: the package (John Williamson, 1989) was associated with the IMF, the World Bank and the US Treasury, not the WTO.

st.2: IFSCA regulates only banking in the IFSCs, while SEBI and IRDAI regulate capital markets and insurance there.
st.3: IBBI was set up under the Companies Act, 2013.

x: Only 1 is correct. 2 is wrong: IFSCA is the unified regulator of banking, capital markets and insurance in IFSCs (and runs FinTech sandboxes). 3 is wrong: IBBI was set up under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016.

st.1: The PCI was first set up on the recommendation of the Second Press Commission.
st.3: The PCI is chaired by a sitting judge of the Supreme Court.
st.4: The PCI has punitive powers over newspapers.

x: Only 2 is correct. 1 is wrong: the PCI (1966, under the 1965 Act) followed the First Press Commission. 3 is wrong: its Chairman is by convention a retired, not sitting, Supreme Court judge (with 28 members). 4 is wrong: it can only warn, admonish or censure.

st.3: Polavaram's Left Main Canal serves mainly Prakasam and Nellore districts.

x: 1, 2 and 4 are correct. 3 is wrong: Polavaram's Left Main Canal goes to East Godavari and Visakhapatnam, not Prakasam and Nellore.

st.3: GRACE satellite studies show the most severe depletion in north-east India.

x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: GRACE studies show the most severe depletion in north-west India (Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan, Delhi), not the north-east.

x: Only 2 is correct. 1 is wrong: AP's position is that the Godavari surplus is NOT yet quantified under the award; the award rests on inter-State agreements.

st.1: Drinking water gets priority over irrigation in the use of water.

x: All three are correct. The order of priority is drinking water > irrigation > power; AP gets 512 TMC and Telangana 299 TMC of KWDT-I's 811 TMC; Polavaram is a national project under Section 90.

st.1: Kerala recorded the lowest Crude Death Rate as per SRS 2024.
st.3: Chhattisgarh has the highest life expectancy at birth as per SRS 2016-20.

x: 2 and 4 are correct. 1 is wrong: the lowest CDR in SRS 2024 is Delhi's, not Kerala's. 3 is wrong: Chhattisgarh has the lowest life expectancy (SRS 2016-20); NCT Delhi has the highest.

x: All three are correct. JSY (2005, under NRHM) replaced the National Maternity Benefit Scheme and gives cash assistance for institutional delivery; wage-loss compensation is PMMVY's purpose.

st.4: The satellite-based DEGURBA estimate of about 63% urban was made by the Economic Advisory Council to the PM.

st.2: Youth unemployment, about 17.5%, was below the national level.

x: Only 1 is correct. 2 is wrong: AP's youth unemployment (about 17.5%) was above, not below, the national level; overall unemployment was 4.1%.

st.2: Anaemia among women in India fell between NFHS-4 and NFHS-5.

x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: anaemia among women rose from about 53% (NFHS-4) to about 57% (NFHS-5).

st.2: In August 2025, Fitch upgraded India's sovereign rating from BBB- to BBB.

x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: the August 2025 upgrade from BBB- to BBB was by S&P, not Fitch.

st.3: Census 2011 was the first Census to collect data through a mobile app.

x: 2 and 4 are correct. 1 is wrong: the 1872 Census was held under Lord Mayo; Ripon presided over the 1881 Census. 3 is wrong: Census 2011 (15th since 1872, 7th after Independence) was paper-based; Census 2027 is the first app-based one.

st.1: LFPR counts only employed persons as a share of the working-age population.
st.2: The Unemployment Rate is unemployed persons as a percentage of the total population.

x: 3 and 4 are correct. 1 is wrong: the labour force in LFPR includes both the employed and the unemployed. 2 is wrong: UR = unemployed ÷ labour force × 100; unemployed ÷ population is the Proportion Unemployed.

st.1: The term 'jobless growth' was coined by Arthur Lewis.
st.3: Employment elasticity is the percentage change in output divided by the percentage change in employment.
st.4: A low employment elasticity means employment grows faster than output.

x: Only 2 is correct. 1 is wrong: the term was coined by Nick Perna, not Arthur Lewis. 3 is wrong: employment elasticity = % change in employment ÷ % change in output. 4 is wrong: a low elasticity means output grows with little rise in employment.

st.3: The term referred to the growth of per capita income rather than of national income.
st.4: The 'Bharat rate of growth' (June 2026) refers to the 3.5% growth of the 1950s to early 1980s.

x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: the Hindu rate (about 3.5%) was the growth of national income; per capita income grew only about 1.37%. 4 is wrong: the 'Bharat rate of growth' is the 8%+ growth hoped for through AI-led 'Reforms 3.0'.

st.1: As per the National MPI (NFHS-5, 2019-21), Kerala has the highest and Bihar the lowest multidimensional poverty.
st.3: Between 2011-12 and 2022-23, rural poverty in Bihar fell from 47.8% to 8.6%.

x: Only 2 is correct. 1 is wrong: Bihar has the highest and Kerala the lowest multidimensional poverty. 3 is wrong: the 47.8% → 8.6% fall in rural poverty was Odisha's, not Bihar's.

st.2: The Feldman-Mahalanobis strategy of the Second Plan gave priority to export promotion.
st.3: The Second Plan had to be cut because of the 1962 war with China.

x: Only 1 is correct. 2 is wrong: the Mahalanobis strategy stressed heavy industry and import substitution, not export promotion. 3 is wrong: the Second Plan (1956-61) was cut by the 1958 foreign-exchange crisis; the 1962 war hit the Third Plan.

st.1: The Eighth Plan fell short of its growth target.
st.3: The average growth over the First to Eleventh Plans was lower than before Independence.

x: Only 2 is correct. 1 is wrong: the Eighth Plan exceeded its target, with industry growing about 8.5% a year. 3 is wrong: the plan-era average (about 4.5%) was far above the pre-Independence rate (about 1%).

st.1: The State Bank of India was formed from the Imperial Bank during the Second Plan period.
st.2: Regional imbalance persisted across States but not within States.

x: Only 3 is correct. 1 is wrong: SBI was formed in 1955, during the First Plan. 2 is wrong: regional imbalance persisted both across and within States.

st.2: The tax net was contracted.

st.3: The Digital Food Currency pilot launched in Puducherry in 2026 runs on UPI money rather than the e-Rupee.

x: Only 1 is correct. 2 is wrong: the e-Rupee is a liability of the RBI; UPI money is a bank liability. 3 is wrong: the Puducherry Digital Food Currency pilot (2026) uses the e-Rupee.

x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: the repo rate lies below the MSF, between the SDF floor and the MSF/bank-rate ceiling.

st.3: The committee set up in December 1997 (report April 1998) was the Committee on the Financial System.

x: Only 2 is correct. 1 is wrong: the 10% CRAR was a Narasimham-II (1998) recommendation. 3 is wrong: Narasimham-II was the Committee on Banking Sector Reforms; the Committee on the Financial System was the 1991 one.

st.3: The base year of CPI-IW was revised from 2016 to 2001 with effect from September 2020.

st.1: Wagner's law holds that public spending rises slower than national income as an economy industrialises.
st.2: Wagner's law is also called the displacement effect.

x: Only 3 is correct. 1 is wrong: Wagner's law holds that public spending rises faster than national income. 2 is wrong: Wagner's is the law of increasing state activity; the displacement effect is Peacock-Wiseman's.

st.2: The Contingency Fund of India is the main account into which government revenues are credited.

x: Only 1 is correct. 2 is wrong: government revenues go into the Consolidated Fund of India, not the Contingency Fund.

st.2: The FRBM escape clause can be invoked only on grounds of war or national security.

x: Only 1 is correct. 2 is wrong: the escape clause also covers national calamity, collapse of agriculture, structural reforms and a sharp fall in output growth; the deviation is capped at 0.5% of GDP.

st.2: The Thirteenth Finance Commission was headed by Y.V. Reddy.
st.3: A Fiscal Council, recommended by the N.K. Singh committee, has been in place since 2018.

x: Only 1 is correct. 2 is wrong: Vijay Kelkar headed the Thirteenth Finance Commission; Y.V. Reddy headed the Fourteenth. 3 is wrong: no Fiscal Council has been set up yet, a common criticism of the FRBM regime.

st.1: A low ratio points to a small informal sector and low tax evasion.
st.3: The World Bank regards 15% as a ceiling beyond which taxation hurts growth.

x: Only 2 is correct. 1 is wrong: a low ratio points to a large informal sector or high evasion. 3 is wrong: the World Bank's 15% is a tipping point (minimum) for sustained growth, not a ceiling.

st.3: Budget deficit is the excess of total expenditure over revenue receipts only.

x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: the budget deficit is total expenditure minus ALL receipts (revenue + capital), not revenue receipts only.

st.1: NIRVIK (Niryat Rin Vikas Yojana), announced in the Budget 2020-21, is an EXIM Bank scheme giving exporters higher insurance cover at a lower premium.
st.3: Enforcing pre-shipment inspection and quality control of exportable goods is an objective of ECGC.

x: Only 2 is correct. 1 is wrong: NIRVIK is an ECGC scheme, not an EXIM Bank one. 3 is wrong: pre-shipment inspection and quality control are the Export Inspection Council's work.

st.1: The rupee is fully convertible on both the current and the capital account.
st.3: FEMA, enacted in 1999, made foreign-exchange violations criminal offences, as FERA had.

x: Only 2 is correct. 1 is wrong: the rupee is fully convertible only on the current account. 3 is wrong: FEMA (in force 1 June 2000) made violations civil offences, unlike FERA's criminal ones.

st.3: FDI in FY 2025-26 was lower than in 2024-25.

x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: AP's FDI rose from $233.14 mn in 2024-25 to $608.59 mn in FY 2025-26.

st.1: Rice yield is below the national average in Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and Tamil Nadu.
st.3: Pulse yields are highest in Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh.

x: Only 2 is correct. 1 is wrong: rice yield in AP, Telangana and Tamil Nadu is above the national average. 3 is wrong: pulse yields are highest in Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat, not Rajasthan.

st.2: NAFIS 2021-22 was conducted by the Reserve Bank of India.

x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: NAFIS is conducted by NABARD, not the RBI.

st.3: The RBI has backed loan waivers as a way to strengthen credit culture.

x: Only 1 is correct. 2 is wrong: the AP scheme was implemented by Rythu Sadhikara Samstha, not NABARD. 3 is wrong: the RBI criticises waivers for moral hazard and hurting credit culture.

st.1: The Government of India sold its stake in NABARD to the RBI in 2019.

x: Only 2 is correct. 1 is wrong: it was the RBI that sold its stake to the Government in 2019, making NABARD fully government-owned.

st.2: Electronic KCCs were introduced on the recommendation of the R.V. Gupta Working Group.
st.4: Short-term KCC credit covers the purchase of tractors and combine harvesters.

x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: electronic KCCs followed the T.M. Bhasin Working Group (R.V. Gupta recommended the KCC itself). 4 is wrong: tractors and combine harvesters are not short-term KCC credit.

st.2: MSP is a legal right of farmers under a Central statute.

x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: MSP is an administrative decision, not backed by any statute.

st.3: Its headquarters is in Mumbai.

x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: FCI is headquartered in New Delhi, not Mumbai.

st.1: After 1991 the role of the government shifted from facilitator to regulator.
st.2: It was announced on 24 July 1991, when P. Chidambaram was the Finance Minister.

x: Only 3 is correct. 1 is wrong: the shift was the reverse, from regulator to facilitator. 2 is wrong: NIP 1991 was announced on 24 July 1991 when Manmohan Singh was the Finance Minister.

st.2: Make in India 2.0 covers only manufacturing sectors.
st.3: Of these, the 15 manufacturing sectors are handled by the Department of Commerce and the 12 services sectors by DPIIT.

x: Only 1 is correct. 2 is wrong: Make in India 2.0 covers 27 sectors, 15 manufacturing and 12 services. 3 is wrong: DPIIT handles the manufacturing sectors and the Department of Commerce the services sectors.

st.2: Penalties under the Act are imposed by the Ministry of Electronics and IT.
st.3: The DPDP Rules have not yet been notified.

st.3: The first-ever Credit Guarantee Scheme for the livestock sector (2023) was launched by NABARD.
st.4: The Credit Guarantee Scheme for livestock is a part of PM-KISAN.

st.2: The subsidy for a Large unit is paid in a single instalment.
st.4: Fixed Capital Investment (FCI) includes the cost of land.

st.1: AP Fiber Grid Phase-I is a 24,000 km IP-MPLS ring whose Network Operations Centre is at Vijayawada.

x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: walking east, north (the Pole Star) is on the left, not the right.

st.3: Indonesia is part of Oceania.

st.3: An anticyclone rotates anticlockwise in the Northern Hemisphere.

st.2: Each village is to have 5-9 Captains, with reservation for women.

st.3: The Court held that Clinically Assisted Nutrition and Hydration (CANH) is basic care, which can never be withdrawn.
